headline: UNDERGROUND BONANZA: DPM Metals hits 58m at 15.28 g/t AuEq deep below Chelopech — resource estimate by year-end
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX/ASX: DPM) reports its best-ever intercepts at the Chelopech Wedge Zone Deep prospect — 58m at 15.28 g/t AuEq located 250m below existing mine infrastructure in Bulgaria. A second hole returned 81m at 8.05 g/t AuEq. An initial mineral resource estimate is targeted for year-end 2026.

headline: MOROCCO MOTHERLODE: Aya Gold & Silver intersects 890 g/t AgEq over 51.5m at Boumadine — PEA update due mid-2026
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) drills 51.5m at 890 g/t silver-equivalent at Morocco's Boumadine project, with a new parallel mineralized structure intersected 70m below current resources — best interval 1,504 g/t AgEq over 19.3m. An updated PEA is expected mid-year as part of an 11-rig, 360,000m drill campaign.

headline: BEST EVER: GR Silver drills 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag at San Marcial — including 8.25m at 8,579 g/t bonanza zone
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) announces its best-ever drill hole at San Marcial in Mexico — 45.1 metres at 1,623 g/t silver with a bonanza interval of 8.25m at 8,579 g/t, confirming the high-grade structural model and extending the 20,000m step-out campaign.

headline: ONTARIO GOLD RUNS BROAD: NexGold intersects 15.21 g/t Au over 20.1m in Goldlund infill program
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSX: NEXG) reports broad high-grade results at the Goldlund deposit in Ontario including 15.21 g/t gold over 20.1m and 5.11 g/t over 21.8m, supporting open-pit resource continuity. The 25,000m infill drill program is now 76% complete.

headline: IRAN DEAL FALTERS: Gold breaks $4,500, silver loses $74 support as ceasefire talks stall
snippet: Gold fell below $4,500 and silver broke $74 support after Iran rejected the US peace proposal and Trump called Tehran's counter-demands 'garbage.' Gold trades at $4,517 today — down 4.7% over the past month but still up 37% year-on-year — while silver has retreated sharply from an $87 peak hit earlier in May.

headline: COPPER VOLATILE: Inflation fears, Iran standoff, and China demand miss slam industrial metals in choppy session
snippet: Copper swung sharply May 21 as bond-market inflation fears collided with US-Iran deal optimism, while Chinese retail sales and industrial production both missed forecasts. Goldman Sachs expects a US copper tariff of at least 25% to be recommended by Commerce Dept in June, adding another layer of uncertainty.

headline: GOLDMAN HOLDS LINE: $5,400 year-end gold target reaffirmed — central banks back buying 60 tonnes per month
snippet: Goldman Sachs reaffirms its $5,400 year-end gold price target despite the metal's 10%+ March correction, citing central bank purchases recovering to an estimated 80 tonnes/month in April. The bank says risks are 'asymmetrically skewed to the upside' and that the March selloff changed nothing structurally.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM -15%: Brazilian court order triggers emergency appeal and 'fake news' counter-campaign
snippet: Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ: SGML) shares dropped 15% after a local Brazilian judge issued an order with a potential US$10 million collateral requirement. The company filed an urgent appeal against what it calls an 'unwarranted' ruling that violates due process, noting the timing coincides with a disinformation campaign against the company despite record Q1 earnings.

headline: NDPR CORRECTS 21%: Rare earth magnet metal pulls back hard after a 105% Q1 run — still up 88% YTD
snippet: NdPr oxide fell to $99.61/kg in April — a 21% monthly decline driven by profit-taking and inventory drawdown after a 105% Q1 surge. Despite the correction, prices remain 88% above January's open as the market enters its second consecutive year of structural supply deficit against rising EV and wind turbine demand.

headline: STOP CHASING $87: Silver retreats to $75 — why the pullback doesn't break the structural bull case
snippet: Silver has pulled back from a May peak near $87 to below $75, with Iran deal optimism and position unwinds driving the move. Analysts argue the structural case — a projected 46 million ounce annual deficit and surging solar and data-centre demand — remains intact for investors with a multi-month time horizon.
